predecessors.name: Median Kingdom
predecessors.text: the Median realm, from northeastern Iran to the Kızılırmak: 'in 550 BC succeeded in defeating the Medes'

successors.name: Kingdom of Macedon
successors.text: the empire Alexander conquered in 334-330: Anatolia, the Levant, Egypt, Mesopotamia, Persia and, to 327, the east under Bessus

ledger.x: 550: Cyrus the Great founds the Achaemenid Empire by defeating the Medes.
550: the Median realm passes to Cyrus.
546: 'Commagene was incorporated into Persia in 546 BC.'
542: Harpagus completes the conquest of Asia Minor.
Page silent: the Cyrus the Great page does not mention Cilicia, but Cliopatria's 540 outline holds it (87 percent) and the page has Harpagus 'finish the conquest of Asia Minor' in 542.
Page undated: 'By 525 BC, Cambyses had successfully subjugated Phoenicia and Cyprus', and the Phoenician fleet made up 'a large part of Cambyses' fleet'.
525 or before: Cyprus passes to Persia.
525: 'In 525 BC, after conquering Egypt, the Achaemenid (Persian) army of Cambyses II seized the Pentapolis'.
493: the Ionian Revolt ends in Persian victory ('lasting from 499 to 493 BC').
479: the Persians are driven from Greece.
Page gives the cause, not the year: the withdrawal from Europe after Sestos (479) and Byzantium (478) was 'allowing Macedonia and the Ionian cities to reassert independence'.
405: Amyrtaeus drives the Persians out of Memphis.
Page silent on the end of the Cyrenaican allegiance; set with the loss of Egypt, to which Libya went in Cliopatria's 383 Thirtieth Dynasty shape.
Page silent: no page opened dates the loss of the Indus.
Page undated: 'Soon after this Egyptian defeat [about 351], Phoenicia, Anatolia and Cyprus declared their independence from Persian rule'; Tennes, king of Sidon, defeated two satraps.
343: the Cyprian rebels are put down.

Page thin: Alexander 'defeated the Persian armies at Granicus (334 BC)' and Issus (333 BC), but neither page says which satrapies fell when; the region is Cliopatria's 337 outline minus its 333 outline.
Page silent on the end of fighting in Anatolia; set with Issus ('at the Battle of Issus in 333 BC').
Page silent: neither the Achaemenid Empire nor the Darius III page mentions Tyre or Gaza.
Page silent on who held Ecbatana: Darius 'fled to Ecbatana and attempted to raise a third army', then 'decided to retreat to Bactria'.
330: Darius III is killed and the empire ends.

wars.name: Revolts against Darius I
wars.outcome: All suppressed within a year: 'By 522 BCE, there were revolts against Darius in most parts of the Achaemenid Empire' and 'Darius was able to suppress and quell all revolts within a year.'

wars.name: Cyrus' conquest of Lydia
wars.outcome: Persian victory at Thymbra and Sardis; the Lydian kingdom annexed in 546 BC (infobox 547).

wars.name: Cyrus' campaigns in Central Asia
wars.outcome: The eastern provinces were taken: the campaigns in the east ran 'between around 545 BC to 540 BC'; the page names peoples and provinces, not states.

wars.name: Persian conquest of Babylon
wars.outcome: Cyrus defeated the Babylonians at Opis and entered Babylon in October 539; Nabonidus surrendered.

wars.name: Persian conquest of Egypt
wars.outcome: Cambyses II won at Pelusium (May 525) and took Memphis; Egypt became a satrapy to 404.

wars.name: Darius I's Scythian campaign
wars.outcome: The army 'was repulsed from Scythia in 513 BC'; Thrace became nominally Persian and Macedonia submitted (about 512-511).

wars.name: Ionian Revolt
wars.outcome: Persian victory; the revolt 'lasting from 499 to 493 BC' was crushed after the Persian army and navy regrouped in 494 (Lade).

wars.name: First Persian invasion of Greece
wars.outcome: Mardonius made Macedon a 'fully subordinate client kingdom of Persia' in 492; the Persians were defeated at Marathon in 490 and withdrew.

wars.name: Second Persian invasion of Greece
wars.outcome: Xerxes razed Athens and 'captured most of Greece', then lost at Salamis (480) and Plataea and Mycale (479) and withdrew.

wars.name: Greek counter-offensive and Peace of Callias
wars.outcome: Sestos (479), Byzantium (478), Ionia freed at the Eurymedon (466), Cyprus contested (478, 451), Egypt (460-454); closed by the 'purported' Peace of Callias of 449, whose terms the page does not give.

wars.name: Revolt of Inaros II
wars.outcome: Persian victory under Megabyzus in 454 BC; Athenian forces besieged for 18 months and wiped out.

wars.name: Egyptian revolt of Amyrtaeus
wars.outcome: Amyrtaeus expelled the Persians from Memphis in 405 and was crowned in 404: Egypt independent for about sixty years.

wars.name: King's Peace (Peace of Antalcidas)
wars.outcome: 'the cities in Asia should belong to him, as well as Clazomenae and Cyprus among the islands'; Ionia and Cyprus returned to the Persians.

wars.name: Artaxerxes III's reconquest of Egypt and the Phoenician and Cypriot revolt
wars.outcome: The attack of about 351 failed and Phoenicia and Cyprus rose; Idrieus reduced Cyprus in 343 and Egypt was reconquered in 343 (Achaemenid Empire page) or 340/339 (Artaxerxes III page).

wars.name: Wars of Alexander the Great against Persia
wars.outcome: Granicus (334), Issus (333), Gaugamela (331), Persepolis burned (330), Darius III killed in July 330 by Bessus, who took the name Artaxerxes V.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a boundary line; the satrapies are named but not mapped, the treaties (Callias 449, Antalcidas 387) name cities and islands, not frontiers.
